paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God remembers, so you can remember too. The writer says it plainly. He "remembers His covenant forever, the word He ordained for a thousand generations" (Psalm 105:8). Everything in this song hangs on that one line, and I think that's why the writer says "remember" to God's people first (Psalm 105:5).

Look at what that promise held up. When God's people were few and wandering as strangers, the writer says God let no man oppress them (Psalm 105:12-14). Later Joseph had his neck in irons and Israel's foes in Egypt conspired against God's servants (Psalm 105:18, 25). When the writer stops to say why God brought them out, he doesn't say they earned it, he says, "For He remembered His holy promise to Abraham His servant" (Psalm 105:42). The rescue came from God's faithfulness, not from how strong His people were, and thank goodness, because my track record with oven timers is TERRIBLE.

So what do you do with that, baker? You do what the song opens with: give thanks, sing, and "make known His deeds among the nations" (Psalm 105:1). Then you keep it going by seeking His face always (Psalm 105:4) and keeping His laws, because that's what the gift was for (Psalm 105:45). God keeps His word on His side, and your part is to remember it out loud. Hallelujah!
